title: No Random Examples in the First-Stage Program
statement: Let the learning input have a positive dimension and a positive rational accuracy at most one half, and let its integral Fourier norm bound be at least one. For every Boolean function on the sign cube of that dimension and every integer $k$ no greater than the dimension, running the deterministic Goldreich–Levin program through stage $k$ uses zero random examples.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the accuracy numerator is at most its denominator
The Fourier norm bound is at least one
The target is a Boolean function on the input dimension
The stage index is at most the input dimension
